saints.name: St. John of Beverley
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: The Northumbrian bishop and teacher who ordained the Venerable Bede and ended his days in the monastery he founded…
biography: Born of noble parents at Harpham in Yorkshire, John studied at Canterbury under Archbishop Theodore and the abbot Adrian, then lived for a time among St. Hilda's community at Whitby. Consecrated bishop of Hexham in 687, he won renown as a preacher and teacher, withdrawing for retreat to Erneshow across the Tyne.

Translated to York in 705, he ordained the young Bede first deacon and then priest. Bede repaid his master by recording his miracles in the Ecclesiastical History — among them the dumb youth with a scabbed head, whom John taught to speak and made whole.

About 717 he resigned his see to Wilfrid the Younger and retired to the monastery he had founded at Inderawuda, the wood of the Deiri, later called Beverley. There he died on 7 May 721. His tomb drew pilgrims for centuries; he was canonized by Benedict IX in 1037, and on 25 October, the day of his translation, Henry V won Agincourt and gave the saint the credit.
saints.knownFor: His holy episcopate and the ordination of the Venerable Bede.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 7 May
